outcome: The provider adapters are easier to read and change safely. Five repeated guards (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Teams) are computed once instead of per branch, and the Telegram callback — previously one ~700-line function handling every button tap — is now a thin dispatcher that builds one context object and hands each kind of tap (question answers, stop, job-permission card, memory/brain reviews, observer, retry, classic permission prompt) to a named handler in its own module. Nothing changed in behaviour: every existing test passes untouched. Complexity: dispatcher 11, largest handler 16 (ceilings 15/25).
title: Channel dispatchers: flatten repeated guards and split the Telegram callback by action kind
